properties.title: CaMeWM: A Causal Medical World Model for Generative Tumor Evolution and Treatment Planning

properties.version_basis: PDF identified by SHA-256 against assignments.json; title page read.

properties.description: Retrospective post-TACE tumor-evolution and regimen-ranking study on 79 episodes with fold-local fitting, cross-fitted AIPW policy evaluation and semi-synthetic estimator validation.
Joint-propensity support gate, response descriptor, deterministic anchor, residual 3D DDPM, fold-local segmenter and response-Cox RMST utility with Monte Carlo ranking over eight sampled worlds.
properties.world_model_status: support-restricted action-conditioned causal generative model, supporting component

properties.algorithm: CaMeWM generated-world pathway (K = 8 worlds per regimen)
properties.world_model_status: supporting component (not_world_model; single pre-to-post transition with assumption-conditional regimen comparison)

properties.population: patients with hepatocellular carcinoma treated with TACE or DEB-TACE
properties.decision: retrospective regimen comparison between two supported regimens

properties.description: 79 outcome-blind eligible episodes (50 TACE, 29 DEB-TACE) from a public collection of 105 patients, patient-level five-fold out-of-fold
Patient-level five-fold out-of-fold evaluation with fold-local fitting and 2,000-resample patient bootstrap

properties.algorithm: Task-matched reimplementation of MeWM action-conditioned generative dynamics
CaMeWM response-Cox utility on observed follow-up states
CaMeWM deterministic anchor only (no residual DDPM)

properties.summary: Mean estimated support of recommended regimens = 0.597 [0.561, 0.634]
AIPW policy gain over observed regimens = 9.6 [0.61, 18.13]

assertions.rationale: A named public collection, the 105 to 99 to 80 to 79 episode construction and regimen definitions are documented.

Supported regimens are compared by RMST over sampled worlds and the frozen policy is evaluated by cross-fitted AIPW with an estimated gain of 9.60 weeks (95 percent CI 0.61 to 18.13), conditional on untestable assumptions.
No irreversibility or ordering constraints are described.
A learned transition from baseline to follow-up CT is scored on 79 out-of-fold episodes.
A learned anchor and residual diffusion is ablated and compared, with near ties against a deterministic 3D U-Net on tumor HU-MAE.
The transition conditions on the regimen and the direct action path ablation shows the largest degradation.
Residual DDPM samples eight worlds per regimen and recommendation stability is checked up to 32 worlds.

Generated follow-up CT is scored against observed follow-up CT on 79 out-of-fold episodes against five baselines.
Only a single pre-to-post transition is evaluated.

capability_assessments.rationale: Core world-model identity (V11) is not met because CaMeWM models only a single pre-to-post TACE transition (state.persistent is partial; authors explicitly note 'a single transition' limits dynamic-policy inference on p.7), so formal capability is honestly classified as not_world_model (supporting causal generative component). Within this single-transition scope, follow-up CT generation is scored against observed follow-up, the direct action path is ablated, and two supported regimens are compared via a stated g-formula target and cross-fitted factual-only AIPW (+9.60 weeks [0.61, 18.13], 79 OOF episodes) conditional on untestable identification assumptions.

gate_assessments.rationale: A named public collection, outcome-blind cohort construction, fold-local fitting of all nuisance models and held-out patients excluded from selection are documented.

Downgraded to unresolved: G02 requires state.persistent, dynamics.temporal, and rollout.one_step_evaluated at evaluation stage. Although single-step factual post-TACE CT generation is scored against observed follow-up on 79 OOF episodes versus five baselines with patient-bootstrap CIs, state.persistent is only partial (single pre-to-post transition without carrying state across steps), and tumor-region fidelity relies on predicted pseudo follow-up masks rather than manual follow-up masks.
A single pre-to-post transition is predicted, so more than one prediction time is not claimed.
Action support is analysed, but alternative-regimen evidence is assumption-conditional with 79 episodes, two regimens and an AIPW interval whose lower bound is 0.61 weeks.
Identification rests on measured exchangeability, positivity and correct censoring adjustment that the data cannot verify, and sensitivity is shown only in simulation.

legacy_cells.B: CaMeWM: A Causal Medical World Model for Generative Tumor Evolution and Treatment Planning
legacy_cells.C: Gao, Huanlong, He, Xuelei, Zhao, Fengjun, He, Xiaowei
legacy_cells.O: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) / liver tumor treated with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE)
legacy_cells.S: For a patient history with support, which represented TACE regimen has higher modeled restricted mean survival time (RMST)?
legacy_cells.V: Rank supported TACE regimens for estimated RMST; select the regimen with the highest Monte Carlo lower-confidence ranking score.
legacy_cells.AI: Baseline and follow-up 3D CT; tumor masks; eight pre-treatment clinical covariates and missingness indicators; joint TACE regimen; survival/event-time data
legacy_cells.AJ: 3D networks: CT/mask encoders; a baseline regimen classifier with three stages (16, 32, 64 channels) and 128-dimensional softmax head; response predictor; deterministic CT anchor; residual 3D denoiser
legacy_cells.AM: Image features are concatenated with clinical covariates and a one-hot regimen in the response predictor.
legacy_cells.AN: Clinical covariates are median-imputed using outer-training-fold medians and paired with binary missingness indicators; AFP is log(1 + AFP)-transformed.
legacy_cells.AZ: Five-dimensional image-derived treatment-response descriptor (relative volume change, lipiodol deposition, necrosis proxy, enhancement reduction, residual viable-tumor proxy); authors call it an inspectable auxiliary code, not a validated biological mediator.
legacy_cells.BD: Two represented complete joint regimens: cisplatin–doxorubicin–mitomycin-C and doxorubicin LC beads; encoded as one-hot regimen; no dose, timing, or duration specified in the action encoding.
legacy_cells.BF: A candidate regimen is eligible only when its fold-local joint propensity is at least η = 0.05.
legacy_cells.BN: Response-factorized SCM/g-formula and support restriction; the residual CT transition is spatially gated to a dilated baseline-tumor envelope (9 × 9 × 9 max-pool).
legacy_cells.BS: Action-conditioned follow-up CT volume generated as a deterministic anchor plus a lesion-local sampled residual; a fold-local segmenter supplies pseudo follow-up masks.
legacy_cells.BT: Five-dimensional response-descriptor predictor; response-Cox survival curve/RMST utility; supported-regimen policy selector.
legacy_cells.BU: Response-Cox model estimates RMST through τ = 156.4286 weeks (36 months); planning ranks each action by mean RMST minus 1.96 × sample SD / √K.
legacy_cells.BV: Joint-regimen cross-entropy; response-descriptor SmoothL1; conditional DDPM noise-prediction MSE plus global L1, confidence-weighted tumor L1, and 3D SSIM losses; clipped stabilized joint-IPTW weighted Cox partial negative log-likelihood.
legacy_cells.CA: Four NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPUs (48 GB); training duration not stated.
legacy_cells.CG: K = 8 sampled follow-up CT worlds per candidate regimen.
legacy_cells.CK: Maximize supported-regimen RMST ranking score R̄(a) − 1.96 sR(a)/√K; only consider regimens with estimated propensity ≥ 0.05.
legacy_cells.CR: IPCW reliability/calibration diagnostics at 12, 24, and 36 months for factual and generated states; authors caution factual calibration does not certify generated-state calibration.
legacy_cells.CV: Consistency/SUTVA and no interference; conditional treatment exchangeability given pre-treatment history; treatment positivity; pre-treatment adjustment; independent censoring through τ.
legacy_cells.CX: No real-data ground truth exists for individual alternate-world CTs. The authors use known-ground-truth semi-synthetic SCM tests for estimator recovery and policy-value behavior; real-image evaluation compares generated transitions with observed factual follow-up CTs.
legacy_cells.DQ: 79 eligible patient episodes (50 TACE; 29 DEB-TACE); source collection contains 105 patients.
legacy_cells.DX: Factual post-TACE CT prediction on 79 paired out-of-fold episodes: CaMeWM tumor HU-MAE 27.145 HU, change-map ΔSSIM 0.528, SSIM 0.618.
legacy_cells.EB: Removing the direct action path degraded normalized tumor MAE from 0.070 to 0.075 and global HU-MAE from 61.102 to 62.239; ablation intervals overlap as noted by authors.
legacy_cells.EC: Factual-only cross-fitted AIPW estimated policy RMST gain +9.60 weeks (95% CI 0.61–18.13); policy ESS 37.4. Authors state this retrospective estimate does not establish prospective clinical benefit.
legacy_cells.EI: Compared with non-WM baselines: CaMeWM vs 3D U-Net factual CT metrics—HU-MAE 27.145 vs 26.944, SSIM 0.618 vs 0.610, ΔSSIM 0.528 vs 0.523. Generated-world survival C-index 0.615 vs IPTW-Cox 0.609; intervals overlap.
legacy_cells.EJ: Compared with the task-matched MeWM* action-conditioned generator: CaMeWM achieved HU-MAE 27.145 vs 62.910, ΔSSIM 0.528 vs 0.074, and SSIM 0.618 vs 0.438.
legacy_cells.EK: Ablations: causal anchor only (removes residual DDPM); without response-code conditioning; without direct action path; without confidence weighting. Removing the direct action path caused the largest reported degradation.
legacy_cells.EL: Pseudo-mask confidence was a weak proxy for OOF tumor-region error (Spearman ρ = 0.20, 95% CI −0.03 to 0.41); the authors do not treat it as an error certificate. They also report small retrospective cohort, only two supported regimens, partition-dependent uncertainty, and no external/prospective validation.
legacy_cells.EM: Support guardrail excludes regimens below propensity 0.05 and the policy abstains if no regimen is supported; lesion-local spatial gate restricts residual edits to the dilated baseline-tumor envelope.
legacy_cells.FB: State is a registered baseline CT–tumor-mask image state plus pre-treatment clinical covariates; transition state is a follow-up CT with an image-derived tumor mask and response descriptor.
legacy_cells.FL: Baseline CT/tumor-mask and clinical encoder plus one-hot regimen → image-space history and response descriptor → deterministic action/response-conditioned CT anchor plus lesion-local residual DDPM → response-Cox RMST utility → propensity-support-filtered candidate comparison and frozen policy evaluated by factual-only cross-fitted AIPW.
legacy_cells.FM: Authors introduce a support-restricted causal medical world model coupling (1) joint-regimen positivity gating, (2) response-grounded anchor–residual diffusion for follow-up CT worlds, and (3) response-Cox RMST utility with cross-fitted factual-only AIPW policy evaluation.
legacy_cells.FN: On 79 paired OOF episodes, CaMeWM achieved CT SSIM 0.618 and ΔSSIM 0.528; generated-world survival C-index 0.615; factual-only AIPW policy gain +9.60 weeks (95% CI 0.61–18.13). Recommendations matched K = 32 for 78/79 patients.
legacy_cells.FO: Small retrospective cohort; only two supported regimens; partition-dependent uncertainty; no external or prospective validation. Identification depends on measured exchangeability, positivity, and censoring assumptions. Pseudo masks and response descriptors are not validated biological mediators; the model does not identify a unique individual cross-world CT, and factual calibration does not certify generated-state calibration.
legacy_cells.FP: Authors describe a future stochastic response-descriptor model that could sample response descriptors jointly with follow-up worlds, and a future calibrated ensemble for simultaneous uncertainty bounds.
legacy_cells.FQ: Authors state that treatment-conditioned generators can reproduce historical treatment allocation rather than interventional disease dynamics; action conditioning or a plausible CT alone does not answer the causal treatment-planning question.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence is retrospective internal OOF evaluation only. The causal interpretation is conditional on untestable measured-exchangeability/positivity and censoring assumptions; semi-synthetic tests do not validate clinical effects. Generated CTs are not verified individual counterfactual scans, the current Monte Carlo score is not a calibrated finite-sample bound, and no prospective clinical benefit is shown.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M4 Action service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M7 Outcome & causal layer; M8 Planner; M9 Safety & governance
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Keep the learned patient/scene simulator separate from the planner objective; constrain candidate actions and report closed-loop decision quality alongside model fidelity.
legacy_cells.FX: PDF pp. 1–30: title and abstract; introduction and related work; methods (Stages I–III, architecture, losses, causal target, support rule, and policy); main results and Tables 1–4; conclusion and limitations; supplementary S1–S22, including assumptions, proofs, implementation protocol, Tables S1–S8, figures/diagnostics, sensitivity and semi-synthetic analyses. PDF p. 31 is empty after a trailing form-feed. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: A:I are omitted to preserve prefilled workbook values. The full text was read; its two-column extraction linearizes some table rows and fragments some equations, so confidence is Medium. Main table values used here are corroborated by adjacent narrative/supplement where available. No workbook edits or external access were performed. Evidence QA: 46/92 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (50%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 82 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 10 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: All 30 PDF pages were read as extracted text. Main Figures 1-2, Tables 1-4 (pp. 3, 7, 8), and Supplementary Tables S1-S8 and Figures S1-S6 (pp. 10, 13, 17, 18, 23-28) were visually inspected directly via rendered page images; plotted curves in Supplementary Figures S1-S6 were inspected qualitatively rather than digitally digitized.
Table 1 to 4 values were transcribed from the rendered tables. Confidence intervals are asymmetric, so the half-width recorded as uncertainty is derived by this reviewer.
Theorems and proofs (Supplement S1 to S9) were read for their statements and stated scope, and their correctness was not checked.
The MeWM row is a task-matched reimplementation by the authors and does not describe the original system.
The text reports Table 1 with CaMeWM in bold for tumor HU-MAE although the 3D U-Net point estimate is lower, which the text calls essentially tied.
Legacy cells were read from the root workbook row (read only). Unlisted columns remain imported-only. Saved API drafts for B039 were not opened.
Schema validity and quote occurrence do not establish semantic correctness. One reviewer pass; no independent human review.
notes: Support-restricted causal medical world model for post-TACE tumor evolution that couples a propensity support gate, a response descriptor, a deterministic anchor, a residual 3D DDPM and a response-Cox RMST utility, with fold-local fitting, cross-fitted AIPW policy evaluation and semi-synthetic known-effect checks. L3 assigned as assumption-conditional causal comparison. It is a supporting component because the state conditions one transition only. Source points: 79 episodes and two regimens, AIPW gain interval 0.61 to 18.13 weeks with ESS 37.4, generated-world C-index tied with a tabular IPTW-Cox, near-chance agreement with observed regimens, pseudo follow-up masks with weak confidence association, point-mass response code, and a reimplemented MeWM baseline.
